items.name: Bitter Sweet Symphony
clues: Sweeping strings that loop again and again. In the video, the singer walks down a London street, bumping into people.
1997, at the height of Britpop.
It made the band famous around the world and was nominated for a Grammy.

The loop came from an orchestral version of a 1960s Rolling Stones song, so for over 20 years Mick Jagger and Keith Richards were named as its writers, and the songwriting royalties went to the Stones' side.
Richard Ashcroft of The Verve, who finally got the rights back in 2019.
The title puts two opposite tastes in front of a piece of orchestral music.

items.name: Uptown Funk
clues: Bright horns, a funky guitar and lots of shouting: impossible not to dance to at a wedding.
Released at the end of 2014, and everywhere in 2015.
It spent 14 weeks at number one in the US.
After a claim that it sounded like an old funk hit, members of the Gap Band were added to its list of songwriters.
A British producer, Mark Ronson, with Bruno Mars singing.
The first word of the title is the opposite of 'downtown'.

items.name: Old Town Road
clues: A banjo loop, a trap beat and a lot of cowboy hats.
Released at the end of 2018; it ruled the summer of 2019.
It went viral on TikTok with the 'Yeehaw Challenge', then spent a then-record 19 weeks at number one in the US.
The beat cost $30 online from a Dutch producer, and it samples a Nine Inch Nails track. Billboard then removed it from its country chart.
Lil Nas X, and a remix with Billy Ray Cyrus.
In the title, he's taking his horse down a road in an old town.

items.name: Shape of You
clues: A marimba-style loop and a love story that starts in a bar.
January 2017.
In December 2021 it became the first song to reach three billion streams on Spotify.
In 2022 the High Court in London ruled that it had not copied a grime artist's song called 'Oh Why'.
A singer-songwriter from Suffolk who builds songs with a loop pedal on stage, and once appeared in Game of Thrones.
The singer says he's 'in love with' this, meaning someone's body.

items.name: Stay With Me
clues: A slow, gospel-style ballad with a choir, asking someone not to leave in the morning.
It won Record of the Year and Song of the Year at the Grammys in 2015.
Its chorus was so close to Tom Petty's 'I Won't Back Down' that Petty and Jeff Lynne were added as co-writers, with a 12.5% share.
Sam Smith, from the debut album In the Lonely Hour.
Three words: a request not to go. The first word is 'Stay'.

items.name: Never Gonna Give You Up
clues: Bouncy 1980s synth-pop, sung in a surprisingly deep voice.
Twenty years later it became an internet joke: you click a link and get this video instead. In 2021 the video passed one billion views on YouTube.
In 2023 the singer sued an American rapper for copying his voice on a new song. They settled out of court.
Rick Astley, produced by Stock Aitken Waterman.
The title is a promise never to abandon someone, in five words.
